thread: Follow a sheet of paper from the papermaker's vat through a print shop and into a book that takes on a life of its own. Along the way the swarm meets watermarks, metal letters, mechanical presses, bindings, and inventive books.

candidates.name: Robert C. Williams Museum of Papermaking
candidates.why: Start with handmade sheets, watermarks, papermaking tools, and paper artifacts; the museum's exhibits and resources trace how fibers become pages.

candidates.name: National Print Museum
candidates.why: Move into a working print shop full of wooden and metal type, typecasters, and elaborate hand and cylinder presses that could become mechanical creatures.

candidates.name: Center for Book Arts
candidates.why: Finish among artists' books, bindings, printmaking, and paper engineering, where a printed sheet can fold into surprising new forms.

candidates.name: Melbourne Museum of Printing
candidates.why: Its sprawling collections cover type, typesetting machines, printing presses, and bookbinding hand tools, with many peculiar mechanisms to inhabit.

candidates.name: The Printing Museum
candidates.why: Papermaking and bookbinding studios sit alongside stone lithography presses, engraving equipment, and collections of letterpress type.

candidates.name: Museum of Printing
candidates.why: Collections and resources explore printing machinery, typography, typewriters, and graphic arts, offering the swarm a workshop of expressive mechanisms.

candidates.name: International Printing Museum
candidates.why: Antique printing machinery, wood type, and book arts workshops offer more ways for letters and presses to come alive.

candidates.name: Hamilton Wood Type & Printing Museum
candidates.why: Wooden letters, type-making equipment, printing history, and an online gallery give the swarm a whole alphabet of shapes to inhabit.
